I've farmed these 7 mu for forty years. My father worked this same soil. Going to college didn't change the fact that I'm a farmer — but it did teach me to read the soil test reports and think about why I do what I do, not just repeat what my father did.

Here is how I see this year.

**Winter wheat (about to manage through to June):**

Last year I pulled roughly 510 kg/mu. The field is in decent shape — I apply straw return after maize, so organic matter has been building. Soil test last spring showed available P adequate, K a bit on the low side, N always needs topping up because our sandy loam leaches.

For wheat I'll use an improved variety — Jimai 22 or similar, same as most neighbors. I'll put down about 22 kg N/mu total: around 10 kg as base fertilizer in a compound (I buy the 18-18-15 or similar blend), and 12 kg as urea topdressing at jointing in early spring. Phosphorus about 9 kg P₂O₅/mu, potassium about 7 kg K₂O/mu — mostly delivered through the compound fertilizer at sowing, because P doesn't move in soil so there's no point topdressing it.

Irrigation: we had a dry autumn last year and I had to water before the ground froze. I plan for 3 irrigations — overwintering if needed, jointing in late March, and grain-filling in May. Well water costs me electricity but it's reliable.

Pesticide: 2 applications usually — one for aphids and powdery mildew around heading, one broadleaf herbicide in early spring if weeds show up. I watch the field before spraying.

Tillage: rotary after maize harvest with the straw chopped in. I don't plough every year — it dries the soil out.

**Summer maize (June to September):**

After wheat I go straight to no-till seeding — saves a pass, keeps moisture, and the residue cover helps. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or Denghai type, whatever the dealer has that neighbors got good results from.

Maize in our area responds to N strongly. I'll aim for about 20 kg N/mu — 6 kg as starter in the compound at seeding, 14 kg as urea side-dressed at the big-flare stage (around 10-12 leaves). Phosphorus 7 kg P₂O₅/mu, potassium 7 kg K₂O/mu, mostly through the compound at planting.

Irrigation: 2 times usually — once after seeding to get a stand if the soil is dry, once at tasseling if July rain is short. Our summers are hot and rain is unreliable.

Pesticide: 2 applications — one for armyworm and borer around the whorl stage, one herbicide after emergence. I've been watching for fall armyworm the last few years; if I see it I spray earlier.

Expected yields: wheat 500 kg/mu, maize 600 kg/mu. Both are realistic for my land and management. Every year I push a little — but I don't gamble on inputs I can't afford back.
